text:
Anya Park: Heads-up: found another compatibility class on the v4 gateway. Clients that interleave http-preface frames with websocket ndjson chunks cause our new parser to produce glitched token boundaries. Minimal repro included.
Rajiv Malhotra: Is this the same as the mixed framing issue we saw last quarter?
Anya Park: Related but different. That one was about an inconsistent upgrade handshake. This is runtime: clients legitimately send short http-ish prefaces mid-stream (proxies doing on-the-fly tunnelling). Our strict v4 streaming decoder treats those prefaces as control frames and splits chunks.
Mei Li: Can we normalize at the gateway by collapsing preface patterns into a single canonical marker? Maybe a lightweight translator that only triggers when pattern matched.
Lisa Gonzalez: Ops constraints again: whatever we add must be toggleable per-tenant, have a clear sunset timeline, and SRE must be able to kill it globally. Also need communication plan and an SLA impact estimate.
Anya Park: Proposal sketch:
- feature: "framing-cohort-bridge" enabled per-tenant
- translator model: sniff-first-256 and only rewrite if regex matches (`^\s*POST\s|^Content-Type:|\r\n\r\n`), otherwise pass-through
- signal: add response header `X-RW-Compat: framing-bridge=v1` when rewrite happens
- telemetry: emit `compat.event=framing_bridge_applied`, `client.version`, `tenant.id`
- rollout: opt-in cohorts -> automated waves gated by metrics -> full removal plan
- kill-switch: `featureflags.gateway.frag.bridge_disable` (global)
Rajiv Malhotra: Performance note: local bench on small scale: p50 +5%, p95 +12%, p99 +25% when many multiplexed streams hit translator. CPU spike observed on CG nodes (~18%). Memory delta negligible.
Mei Li: Sniffing-first approach sounds good. We should micro-optimize the regex and keep a small finite-state machine rather than full regex for perf. Also consider a short cache that remembers known-good client fingerprints to skip sniffing on subsequent connections.
Lisa Gonzalez: How long do we plan to keep the bridge? We need a firm deprecation timeline to include in tenant notices and legal.
Anya Park: Draft timeline:
- Week 0: Canary + internal tenants opt-in (2 weeks monitoring)
- Week 2-6: Phase 1 waves: 5% -> 25% -> 50% (telemetry gates at each step)
- Week 6-12: Grace opt-in window for remaining affected tenants, in-console banners + emails
- Week 12: Final shutoff announced (90 days notice) -> Removal at Week 24
- Emergency rollback always available via kill-switch and immediate config flip
Mei Li: Tests required:
- streaming boundary integrity (varied chunk sizes)
- reconnect semantics + KV cache resume
- proxy-interop (grpc-web, http-tunnel)
- fuzz harness that injects random preface bytes
- perf harness for multiplex levels 8/32/128
Rajiv Malhotra: Also add a migration aid: a small SDK helper that normalizes framing on the client if they opt to upgrade. Could reduce total tenants that need bridge. We can ship as a reference snippet.
Anya Park: Sample gateway rule (YAML-like):
```
route: /v4/*
compat:
  name: framing-cohort-bridge
  mode: tenant-opt-in
  sniff_bytes: 256
  emit_header: true
  tenant_allowlist: [t-77, t-99]
rollback_flag: gateway.frag.bridge_disable
```
Lisa Gonzalez: Communication plan:
- Step 1: In-console banner for detected affected tenants (auto-detect)
- Step 2: Targeted email to tenants with >5000 req/day and any compat events
- Step 3: Public deprecation page and support KB with migration steps + SDK snippet
- Step 4: Legal checks + data residency note if we route via additional proxies
legal-bot: Note: any automated rewrites that persist payload shapes may have compliance implications for signed payloads. Ensure we document that the bridge does not modify message contents beyond framing normalization. Also include audit logs for rewrites.
Mei Li: Good catch. We'll add an immutable hash of original frame boundaries to logs (opaque) so support can audit without exposing payload.
Rajiv Malhotra: Telemetry gates: abort if any of the following in a wave:
- translator.error-rate > 0.5% for 30m
- p99 latency regression > 15% vs baseline
- increase in 5xxs > 0.2% absolute
Anya Park: infra-bot, schedule a canary with the above metrics and gates?
infra-bot: Canary job created: gateway-framing-cohort-canary at 2025-03-03T09:00:00Z (CI#5123). Monitors: gateway.cpu, request.latency.p99, compat.event.rate, translator.error-rate.
Lisa Gonzalez: I'll draft the tenant-facing copy and a suggested timeline for support handoffs. Recommend we include a small self-service toggle in the console for tenants to opt-in/out.
Mei Li: I'll build the translator as a pluggable module with a narrow public surface so we can drop it cleanly. Also will add a lightweight LRU fingerprint cache to avoid repeated sniff costs.
Rajiv Malhotra: I'll pair with Mei on perf tuning and add flamegraph runs to the canary playbook.
Anya Park: I'll write the RFC follow-up with explicit rollback criteria, telemetry queries, and the notice cadence. We'll reconvene in 48 hours to finalize. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
